description: ZENORA is a team of five passionate innovators exploring the world of orbital missions and space technology. We aim to develop an innovative and interactive Space Mission Design Game through creativity, teamwork, and engineering.
summary:
ZENORA – Space Mission Lab: Design Beyond the Horizon

ZENORA is an interactive, web-based space mission design and simulation platform developed to make space exploration and mission planning m ore accessible, engaging, and educational. It transforms complex mission-design concepts into an interactive learning experience where users can design missions to Low Earth Orbit, the Moon, and Mars by configuring spacecraft systems, payloads, launch vehicles, budgets, and mission durations.

The platform provides mission feasibility analysis, spacecraft system configuration, orbital simulations, mission comparisons, campaign-based challenges, safety and compliance reviews, and collaborative team missions. It also integrates NASA's Near-Earth Object (NEO) Web Service to allow users to explore real asteroid data.

By combining interactive simulation, real NASA data, and collaborative learning, ZENORA encourages users to understand the engineering challenges, resource trade-offs, and decision-making involved in space exploration. Its goal is to inspire the next generation of space explorers, engineers, and mission designers through an engaging virtual space mission laboratory.
details:
ZENORA – Space Mission Lab is an interactive, browser-based educational platform designed to help students explore the engineering concepts behind space mission planning and spacecraft systems.

The platform provides a guided mission-design experience where users can create and configure missions to destinations such as Low Earth Orbit (LEO), the Moon and Mars. Users can select launch capabilities, payload mass, mission duration, budget, scientific instruments, power architecture, communication systems and mission priorities.

ZENORA includes illustrative feasibility checks, resource estimates and mission comparisons to help users understand the engineering trade-offs involved in designing a space mission. It also features a mission campaign with challenges and achievements, mission events and contingency activities, a mission assurance checklist, a saved mission library and downloadable mission reports. Its collaborative mission room supports up to four participants with real-time updates.

A key feature is the Orbit Lab, which integrates NASA's Near-Earth Object Web Service (NeoWs) API. Users can retrieve asteroid information for a selected date range of up to seven calendar days and explore close-approach dates, miss distances, relative velocities, estimated diameters and potentially hazardous object classifications. This connects the learning experience with authentic NASA open data.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ZENORA aims to make space mission engineering more accessible and engaging, especially for students and beginners. It encourages systems thinking, problem-solving, scientific curiosity and an understanding of resource management. By combining interactive mission planning, guided learning, collaboration and real NASA data, the platform provides an accessible environment for exploring space science and engineering.

Technology and Tools Used

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS and JavaScript
  • Visualisation: HTML Canvas 2D
  • Backend: Node.js and Express.js
  • Real-time communication: Socket.IO
  • External data integration: NASA NeoWs REST API
  • Development environment: Visual Studio Code
  • Deployment: Render

Creativity and Design Considerations

The creative aspect of ZENORA is the integration of mission planning, educational simulation, guided challenges, real-world asteroid data and collaborative activities into one workspace. During development, our team considered accessibility, ease of use, educational value, interface design, performance, data integration and the importance of presenting engineering estimates responsibly.

ZENORA is an educational simulator, not certified spacecraft engineering software or flight software. Its purpose is to inspire learners to understand the complexity and possibilities of space exploration.
